terms.label: Active Fire Protection
terms.definition:
method(s) used to reduce or prevent the spread and effects of fire (3.138), heat or smoke (3.389) by virtue of detection and/or suppression of the fire and which require a certain amount of motion and/or response to be activated
EXAMPLE:The application of agents (e.g. halon gas or water spray) to the fire or the control of ventilation and/or smoke.
Note 1 to entry: Compare with the terms passive fire protection (3.328) and suppression system (3.418).

terms.definition: Aktiv brandsikring omfatter alle tekniske installationer og systemer, der bruges til at registrere, advare om, og bekæmpe brand i en bygning. Det er udstyr, der reagerer aktivt ved brand

terms.label: Compartment-Area - Floor area
terms.definition: Summen af bruttoarealerne for samtlige etager, herunder kældre og udnyttelige tagetager samt altanlukninger, udestuer, forbindelsesgange og lignende. I forbindelse med brandforhold må der ikke foretages fradrag, jf. BR18 § 455, stk. 3 nr. 1, 4 og 5 samt stk. 4, som alene må benyttes ved beregning af bebyggelsesprocent.

terms.label: Fire compartment area
terms.definition: the area of the largest floor of the building. If the building has interconnected spaces between floors (atriums, openings, type 2 staircases, etc.), the areas of all interconnected floors shall be added together when determining the area of the fire compartment. When the maximum area of a fire compartment is exceeded, two or more separate fire compartments shall be formed, separated by fire compartment walls and/or floors. If there are rooms of different purposes or rooms that are dangerous in terms of explosion and fire in a fire compartment, the area of the fire compartment shall be determined according to the purpose of the rooms occupying more than 50% of the total area of the rooms. If there are rooms of different purposes in a fire compartment, not exceeding 50% of the total area of the rooms, the maximum area of the fire compartment Fg shall be determined according to the indicators of the purpose that occupies the largest part of the fire compartment.

terms.label: Fire compartment
terms.definition: Part of one or more buildings designated as a maximum fire expansion area

terms.label: fire-sub-compartment_area
terms.definition: part of a fire compartment intended to restrict the spread of smoke and further restrict the spread of fire

terms.label: Area of refuge space
terms.definition: A refuge area must have a value, in m2, of no less than the effective area of the sites it serves, multiplied by the index 0.2.

rows.label: AreaTriplex (1)

terms.label: Area of triplex compartment
terms.definition: the cumulative gross area of the building layers that form the triplex, measured between the inner surfaces of the compartment boundaries

rows.label: AreaTriplex (2)
rows.interpretation: Same mappings as AreaFireCompartment

terms.label: Area of triplex compartment
terms.definition: the cumulative gross area of the building layers that form the triplex, measured between the inner surfaces of the compartment boundaries

terms.label: Automatic Fire Alarm system
terms.definition: Anlæg, der indeholder ABA-central og detektorer, som ved detektering af røg-, varme- eller flammeudvikling automatisk tilkalder redningsberedskabet, samt eventuelt alarmtryk, der ved manuel aktivering tilkalder redningsberedskabet. Brandtekniske installationer kan kobles til et ABAanlæg, og ABA-anlægget vil derved være det styrende anlæg for de tilkoblede anlæg.

terms.label: Automatic warning system
terms.definition: Anlæg, der via en tone eller en talt besked varsler personer om en utilsigtet hændelse, herunder brand. Varslingsanlæg kan aktiveres manuelt (internt varslingsanlæg) eller automatisk via et ABA-anlæg (automatisk varslingsanlæg).

rows.label: AutomaticFireExtinguishSystem
rows.interpretation: Is this targeting sprinklers or is this more generic and would others also apply?

terms.label: Automatic sprinkler system
terms.definition: Anlæg, der kontrollerer, dæmper eller slukker en brand ved brug af vand som slukningsmiddel. Et sprinkleranlæg består af vandforsyning, alarmventiler og rørsystem med sprinklere. Sprinklere er armaturer, der ved hjælp af spredeplader fordeler den dimensionerede vandtilstrømning på en forudbestemt måde over et bestemt areal. Sprinklere aktiveres oftest ved, at en væskefyldt glasbulb eller smelteled, som er placeret så den blokerer for vandtilstrømningen, opvarmes af branden og brydes ved en given temperatur. Sprinklere kan også være uden glasbulb eller smelteled, og vil da blive aktiveret ved ABA-detektering af røg eller flammer.

terms.label: Sprinkler systems (automatic)
terms.definition: A piping system of the required diameter installed in the building, with sprinkler heads installed at specific intervals. The piping is connected to control valves with alarm devices and a mechanical water supply system.

terms.label: Building

terms.label: Structure

terms.label: Building layer

terms.label: Building storey
terms.definition: The space in a building from the floor surface of the premises to the floor surface of the premises above (upper floor – to the top of the attic floor insulation or the top of the roof covering).

terms.label: building layer
terms.definition: part of a building consisting of one or more rooms, where the tops of the finished floors or of the ground level of two adjacent rooms do not differ in height by more than 1.5 m

terms.label: Calculated altitude
terms.definition: The calculated altitude depends on the purpose of the building [m]. The numerical value is specified in Table 1 of Annex 3 to the Basic Fire Safety Requirements.

terms.label: Ceiling
terms.definition: building element covering the subsurface of the floor or roof and its supporting structure, consisting of suspensions, fixings and any insulation material. The ceiling can be attached directly to the building’s structural elements or be a suspended ceiling

terms.label: Suspended ceiling
terms.definition: Suspended or self-supporting celing

terms.label: Suspended ceiling
terms.definition: Loft placeret under loftsbeklædningen som ikke nødvendigvis opfylder kravene til den indvendige loftsbeklædning.

terms.label: Suspended ceilings
terms.definition: ceilings that are suspended or otherwise fixed and intended solely to increase the fire resistance of a specific structural element (e.g., floor, ceiling, or roof).

terms.label: Collective covered car park

Is it correct to assume that the type is valid if at least one space has this assigned? Can a compartment have multiple types? The “PARKING” predefined type cannot be set at the same time as the “FIRESAFETY” predefined type.

terms.label: Compartment-type:Parking

terms.label: Compartment-type:Single

terms.label: Compartment-type:Technical

terms.label: Triplex

terms.label: Escape route
terms.definition: Route die begint in ruimte voor personen, alleen voert over vloeren, trappen of hellingbanen en eindigt op een veilige plaats, zonder dat gebruik moet worden gemaakt van een lift

terms.label: Primary Evacuation route
terms.definition: Flugtvej, som personer intuitivt vil søge imod ved evakuering, typisk den normale adgangsvej til en bygning eller et rum.

terms.label: Escape route
terms.definition: Route that starts in a space for people, only runs over floors, stairs or ramps and ends in a safe place, without the need to use a lift

terms.label: Internal escape route
terms.definition: Horizontal or vertical communication within a building which, under the terms of this regulation, provides safe conditions for the evacuation of its occupants. Horizontal evacuation routes may be corridors, antechambers, atriums, galleries or, in large spaces, walkways explicitly marked on the floor for this purpose, which comply with the conditions of this regulation. Vertical evacuation routes may be stairs, ramps, or inclined stairs and escalators, which comply with the conditions of this regulation. Evacuation routes may be protected or unprotected. Protected evacuation routes may be enclosed (interior) or exterior. Unprotected evacuation routes are those that do not fully or partially meet the regulatory conditions for protected routes, although they may be authorised under the conditions set out in this regulation.

terms.label: Fire compartment
terms.definition: a closed space in a building (a room or group of rooms) separated from other parts of the same building by structural elements with a specified fire resistance rating, during which time a fire can be extinguished or prevented from spreading to other parts of the building.

terms.label: Fire Resistance
terms.definition: (this content has copy right, will be removed after WIP stage)  “ability of a test specimen (3.428) to withstand fire (3.138) or give protection from it for a period of timeNote 1 to entry: Typical criteria used to assess fire resistance in a standard fire test (3.180) are fire integrity (3.157), fire stability (3.179)and thermal insulation (3.435).Note 2 to entry: “Fire resistant” (adj.) refers only to this ability.Note 3 to entry: The term "fireproof" has been used to describe buildings with non-combustible (3.315) structural elements and high levels of fire resistance, but this is a deprecated term. The term is often misunderstood to mean an absolute or unconditional property, and therefore the use of the term "fireproof" is inappropriate and misleading.” https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#iso:std:iso:13943:ed-4:v1:en:term:3.165

terms.label: Fire resistance
terms.definition: Det tidsrum, hvor en bygningsdel under brandpåvirkning kan opretholde sin ydeevne i form af f.eks. bæreevne eller adskillende funktion

terms.label: Fire Resistance
terms.definition: the ability of a building structure or element (construction product) to withstand specified loads and/or to maintain thermal insulation properties and/or to remain homogeneous (sealed, crack-free) during a specified period of time in a standardised fire resistance test

terms.label: Fire Resistance
terms.definition: Ability of a structure, part of a structure or element to perform its intended functions (load-bearing function and/or compartmentalisation function) for a specific load level, when subjected to a specific fire situation and for a specified period of time.

rows.label: FireResistanceBuilding
rows.interpretation: Need to define a string or pattern of allowed values. This is NOT merely a number

terms.label: Fire resistance rating of the Building
terms.definition: Buildings and fire compartments of buildings, taking into account their fire load categories and the fire resistance of the structural elements used to build them, are divided into buildings and fire compartments of fire resistance levels I, II, III.

terms.label: HorizontalRoute
terms.definition: Horizontal communication in a building that provides safe conditions for the evacuation of its occupants. Horizontal evacuation routes may be corridors, antechambers, atriums, galleries, or, in large spaces, walkways explicitly marked on the floor for this purpose, which comply with the conditions of the Technical Regulations. Evacuation routes may be protected or unprotected. Protected evacuation routes may be enclosed (interior) or exterior.

terms.label: Protected lobby
terms.definition: Independent fire compartment, with a degree of resistance and smoke control systems, which generally establishes communication between two spaces with the aim of ensuring the temporary protection of one of them or preventing the spread of fire between them.

terms.label: Refuge space
terms.definition: A space within a building, temporarily safe, specially equipped with protective measures, so that people are not exposed to the direct effects of a fire in the building.

terms.label: VerticalRoute
terms.definition: Vertical communication in a building that provides safe conditions for the evacuation of its occupants. Vertical evacuation routes may be stairs, ramps, or stairs and inclined escalators, which comply with the conditions of the Technical Regulations. Evacuation routes may be protected or unprotected. Protected evacuation routes may be enclosed (interior) or exterior.

terms.label: Ancillary function

terms.label: Assembly function

terms.label: Assembly function for child care

terms.label: Detention function

terms.label: Educational function

terms.label: Functional usage

terms.label: Health care function

terms.label: Health care function: with bed area
terms.definition: Health care function with bed area

terms.label: Industrial function

terms.label: Industrial function: light industrial function
terms.definition: Industrial function where activities take place in which the staying of persons plays a subordinate role

terms.label: Industrial function: light industrial function for growing, cultivating or storing crops or similar products
terms.definition: Light industrial function in which cultivating or storing crops is the main purpose

terms.label: Industrial function: light industrial function for keeping animals

terms.label: Office function

terms.label: Remaining functional use

terms.label: Remaining functional use: for parking motor vehicles
terms.definition: Remaining functional unit intented for parking motor vehicles

terms.label: Remaining functional use: other passenger transport function:
terms.definition: Remaining functional unit intended for the arrival or departure of vehicles for thetransport of passengers by road, railway, waterway or air

terms.label: Residential function

terms.label: Residential function with care
terms.definition: Residential function where professional care is provided to residents in the context of a combination of residence and care, organised by health care providers, in a residential function intended and equipped for that purpose;

terms.label: Residential function: caravan
terms.definition: Residential function on a plot intended for a caravan

terms.label: Shop function
terms.definition: Functional unit for trading materials, goods or services

terms.label: Sports function
terms.definition: Functional unit for playing sports

terms.label: Structure other than a building
terms.definition: Building or part thereof, insofar as it is not a building or part thereof

terms.label: Temporary accomodation function
terms.definition: Functional unit intended to provide recreational or temporary accommodation to persons

terms.label: Gross area of a floor or fraction
terms.definition: Total surface area of a given floor or fraction, delimited by the outer perimeter of the exterior walls and the axes of the interior walls separating that fraction from the others

terms.label: High Rise building

terms.label: High-rise building

terms.label: Hose reel
terms.definition: A fire hose reel is a flexible hose that is connected to a hydrant in order to extinguish a fire. It is often supported by a reel and the ensemble is known as a hydrant or reel depending on the region

terms.label: Intended use of the building
terms.definition: The purpose of a building is considered to be the intended use of the building as specified in the public register, provided that the building complies with the mandatory requirements for safety and the activities (technological processes) planned (carried out) therein, as set out in the normative documents on building safety and purpose. When changing the purpose of a building, a building permit is required in the case specified in Article 27(1)(6) of the Construction Law. The composition of a building purpose change project is specified in STR 1.04.04:2017 “Building design, project expertise.”

terms.label: Internal wall
terms.definition: Structure which separates two enclosed spaces in a building that are accessible to people, including parts of that structure connected to other structures insofar as those parts affect the compliance of the partition with a regulation under or pursuant to this decree

terms.label: Listed property
terms.definition: Monuments classified under Law No. 107/2001 of September 8

terms.label: Exclusive Occupancy Type
terms.definition: Depending on their use, buildings and premises may be for exclusive use when they are integrated into a single type of occupancy.

terms.label: Mixed Occupancy Type
terms.definition: Depending on their use, buildings and premises may be mixed-use when they incorporate several standard occupancy.

terms.label: Occupancy (type of)
terms.definition: Classification given by the dominant use of any building or enclosure, or of each of its parts, in accordance with the provisions of Art. 8 of Legal Regime - Fire Safety in Buildings

terms.label: OccupancyType I - Residential Building
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings intended for single-family or multi-family housing, including common access spaces and non-residential areas reserved for the exclusive use of residents

terms.label: OccupancyType II - Garages and Car Parks
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings intended exclusively for the collection of vehicles and their trailers off the public highway, or enclosed open-air spaces for the same purpose

terms.label: OccupancyType III - Administrative
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings where administrative, customer service or service activities are carried out, namely offices, public offices, courts, registry offices, service counters, notaries, offices of liberal professionals, research spaces not dedicated to teaching, security and rescue force posts, excluding repair and maintenance workshops

terms.label: OccupancyType IV - Schools
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings open to the public, where education, teaching and training activities are carried out or recreational or educational activities are carried out for children and young people, which may or may not include resting or sleeping areas for participants in these actions and activities, namely schools at all levels of education, nurseries, kindergartens, training centers, leisure centers for children and young people and youth centers

terms.label: OccupancyType IX - Sports and Leisure Facilities
terms.definition: Buildings, parts of buildings and enclosures, whether or not they are open to the public, used for sports and leisure activities, namely stadiums, riding arenas, hippodromes, velodromes, autodromes, motodromes, karting arenas, playing fields, camping and caravan parks, sports halls, swimming pools, water parks, skating rinks, gyms and saunas

terms.label: OccupancyType V - Healthcare and Nursing Homes
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings open to the public, intended for the performance of diagnostic procedures or the provision of healthcare, with or without hospitalization, for the support of elderly people or those with physical or mental disabilities, or where activities dedicated to such individuals are carried out, namely hospitals, clinics, medical offices, polyclinics, medical dispensaries, health centers, diagnostic centers, nursing centers, hemodialysis centers, or physical therapy centers, clinical analysis laboratories, as well as nursing homes, shelters, residences, shelters, and day centers with activities intended for the elderly

terms.label: OccupancyType VI - Public Entertainment and Assembly
terms.definition: Buildings, parts of buildings, itinerant or temporary venues and open-air venues that receive the public, intended for shows, public meetings, the showing of audiovisual media, dances, games, conferences, lectures, religious worship and exhibitions, whether or not they can be multipurpose, multipurpose and carry out the above activities on a non-permanent basis, namely theaters, cinemas, coliseums, bullrings, circuses, gambling halls, dance halls, nightclubs, bars with live music, recording studios, auditoriums, conference rooms, religious temples, multi-purpose pavilions and exhibition venues not classifiable under Occupancy Type X

terms.label: OccupancyType VII - Hotels and Restaurants
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings, receiving the public, providing temporary accommodation or carrying out food and beverage activities, whether or not under exclusive occupation, namely those intended for tourist developments, local accommodation, where applicable, food and beverage establishments, dormitories and, when not part of a school establishment, student residences and vacation camps, excluding camping and caravanning sites, which are considered to be occupancy type IX spaces

terms.label: OccupancyType VIII - Commercial Establishments and Transport Terminal
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings open to the public, occupied by commercial establishments where materials, products, equipment, or other goods are displayed and sold for consumption outside the establishment, or occupied by stations providing access to road, rail, sea, river, or air transportation, including intermodal terminals, which serve as a connecting space between public roads and these modes of transportation, with the exception of open-air boarding platforms

terms.label: OccupancyType X - Museums and Art Galleries
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings, whether or not they are open to the public, intended for the exhibition of items of historical and cultural heritage or for scientific, cultural or technical exhibition, demonstration and dissemination activities, namely museums, art galleries, oceanariums, aquariums, zoological or botanical park facilities, exhibition spaces intended for scientific and technical dissemination, provided that they do not fall under type VI and IX occupancies

terms.label: OccupancyType XI- Libraries and Archives
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings, whether or not they are open to the public, intended for document archiving, which may or may not make documents available for consultation or viewing on site, including libraries, media libraries, and archives

terms.label: OccupancyType XII- Industrial Facility, Workshops and Warehouses
terms.definition: Buildings, parts of buildings or open-air enclosures, not normally open to the public, used for industrial activities or the storage of materials, substances, products or equipment, repair workshops and all services ancillary or complementary to these activities

rows.label: OccupancyType (Compartment)
rows.interpretation: The PT occupancies represent a fixed list, but applicable to buildings or parts of buildings. Are these parts compartments? Or Rooms?

terms.label: Exclusive Occupancy Type
terms.definition: Depending on their use, buildings and premises may be for exclusive use when they are integrated into a single type of occupancy.

terms.label: Mixed Occupancy Type
terms.definition: Depending on their use, buildings and premises may be mixed-use when they incorporate several standard occupancy.

terms.label: Occupancy (type of)
terms.definition: Classification given by the dominant use of any building or enclosure, or of each of its parts, in accordance with the provisions of Art. 8 of Legal Regime - Fire Safety in Buildings

terms.label: OccupancyType I - Residential Building
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings intended for single-family or multi-family housing, including common access spaces and non-residential areas reserved for the exclusive use of residents

terms.label: OccupancyType II - Garages and Car Parks
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings intended exclusively for the collection of vehicles and their trailers off the public highway, or enclosed open-air spaces for the same purpose

terms.label: OccupancyType III - Administrative
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings where administrative, customer service or service activities are carried out, namely offices, public offices, courts, registry offices, service counters, notaries, offices of liberal professionals, research spaces not dedicated to teaching, security and rescue force posts, excluding repair and maintenance workshops

terms.label: OccupancyType IV - Schools
terms.definition: Buildings or parts of buildings open to the public, where education, teaching and training activities are carried out or recreational or educational activities are carried out for children and young people, which may or may not include resting or sleeping areas for participants in these actions and activities, namely schools at all levels of education, nurseries, kindergartens, training centers, leisure centers for children and young people and youth centers

terms.label: OccupancyType IX - Sports and Leisure Facilities

terms.label: Number of occupants of a compartment
terms.definition: For rooms not accessible to the public, the number of users is at least equal to the surface area of the compartment/10. For rooms accessible to the public, the number of users is at least equal to the surface area of the compartment/3. If the number of users can be accurately determined based on fixed furniture, this surface area may be deducted. The number of users is then the sum of the accurately determined number and the number calculated based on the reduced surface area.

terms.label: Number of Occupants per Compartment
terms.definition: Det antal personer, som den enkelte brandmæssige enhed er indrettet til, og som bl.a. angives på brandplaner og på pladsfordelingsplaner. Benyttes også som betegnelse for det dimensionsgivende antal personer, f.eks. angivet ved antal personer pr. m2 , som lægges til grund ved dimensionering af bredde af flugtveje, flugtvejspassager og døre til flugtveje samt ved evakueringsberegninger ved brandteknisk dimensionering.

rows.label: Occupants (Room)
rows.interpretation: LT: OccupantsOfRoom in Miro, but not in Notion

terms.label: Partial coefficients for the fire safety assessment of a building
terms.definition:
G1…G8 – partial coefficients for the fire safety assessment of a building, depending on the fire safety systems installed in the building and the capabilities of the fire rescue service; their numerical values are given in Table 2 of Annex 3 (https://e-seimas.lrs.lt/portal/legalAct/lt/TAD/TAIS.388658/asr).
The values of the partial coefficients G3 and G4 shall only be applied with the approval of the state fire rescue service.

terms.label: Self-closing
terms.definition: The door is provided with a self-closing mechanism (either triggered or always closing)

rows.label: SmokeAndHeatExtraction
rows.interpretation: Per space? For the full compartment?

terms.label: Smoke and heat ventilation equipment
terms.definition: A system designed to improve the removal of combustible gases and heat from a building in the event of a fire. Smoke and heat are removed by mechanical ventilation equipment and/or natural convection.

terms.label: Reaction to fire; smoke class
terms.definition: Smoke class determined according to NEN-EN 13501-1.

terms.label: space
terms.definition: covered, completely or partially enclosed by walls

terms.label: Spaces
terms.definition: Interior and exterior areas of buildings or enclosures.

terms.label: Teaching Zone
terms.definition: (this content has copy right, will be removed after WIP stage) zone (3.1.9) where a group of pupils or students are taught or study together https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#iso:std:iso:6707:-4:ed-1:v1:en:terms:3.3.23

rows.label: UsableAreaFireCompartment
rows.interpretation: The measurement method is described in the Dutch regulation. It is different from the NetFloorArea as defined by buildingSMART

terms.label: Fire compartment usable area
terms.definition: The usable area of a firecompartment is measured at floor level, between the rising partitions that enclose the room or group of rooms in question. The following are not taken into account when determining the GO: — the area of parts of floors above which the net height is less than 1.5 m, with the exception of floors under stairs, ramps, etc.; — a lift shaft; — a stairwell, ring hole or void, if its area is greater than or equal to 4 m2; — a free-standing building structure (other than a staircase) if its horizontal cross-section is greater than or equal to 0.5 m2; — a service shaft, if its horizontal cross section is greater than or equal to 0.5 m2; — a load-bearing internal wall.

rows.label: UsableAreaLiftShaft
rows.interpretation: The measurement method is described in the Dutch regulation. It is different from the NetFloorArea as defined by buildingSMART
